pool.text: King Mindon founded Mandalay as the new royal capital of the Konbaung dynasty.
The British Empire annexed the kingdom after conquering Mandalay.
Rudyard Kipling wrote a famous poem called Mandalay about the location.
A severe plague caused about one-third of the population to flee the city.
The poem Mandalay was set to music by composer Oley Speaks.
Bithia Mary Croker wrote a novel titled The Road to Mandalay.
An American silent film was released based on the novel.
The Imperial Japanese Army Air Service carried out an extensive assault during conquest.
Mandalay became a part of the newly independent Union of Burma.
Mandalay celebrated its centennial with a festival at Mandalay Hill.
Looted palace treasures were returned to Burma as a gesture of goodwill.
A massive fire razed more than 6,000 houses and public buildings.
Another fire destroyed 2,700 buildings and made many people homeless.
The reconstruction project of the palace was completed.
The Mandalay Daily newspaper began publishing by the development committee.
Mandalay International Airport was built at a cost of US$150 million.
Pop singer Robbie Williams released a single called The Road to Mandalay.
The public health care system consisted of over 1,000 doctors and 2,000 nurses.
A major fire destroyed Yadanabon Market, the city's second largest market.
A magnitude 7.7 earthquake with an epicenter northwest of the city caused extensive damage.
